text: docwright（DSH Web/CLI 插件）：按 pack 生成并校验结构化项目文档。它注册文档 pack 查询、生成、参数提取、文档校验和链状态查询工具，并加载内置 pack。生成流程依据 schema 与规则检查结果，未通过时进入修复循环，保存 JSON、Markdown 和可重放的校验回执。用户也可从素材提取有出处的参数，在设置页维护插件参数。适合需要按模板产出和复核项目文档的 DSH 用户。生成需要宿主配置可用的 LLM provider；素材和产物默认位于工作区 references/ 与 output/。

docwright (DSH Web/CLI plugin) generates structured documents from packs. It registers tools for pack discovery, generation, parameter extraction, validation, and chain status. It checks schemas and rules, repairs drafts, and saves JSON, Markdown, and receipts. A host LLM provider is required.
想让 DSH 按固定格式生成项目文档。
有没有能检查生成文档并自动修正问题的 DSH 工具？
我想把已有材料里的参数提取出来，并能核对出处。
如何重新验证已有 JSON 文档并查看校验回执？
I need DSH to generate structured project documents from reusable packs.
Can DSH validate a draft, repair rule violations, and save a replayable receipt?
docwright 的功能「按 pack 生成文档」：调用 doc_generate 选择 pack 和素材；插件按 schema 与规则校验并修复结果，保存 JSON、Markdown 和回执。
docwright 的功能「校验和回放文档回执」：调用 doc_validate 指定工作区内的 JSON 产物和 pack，重新运行对应规则并比较产物哈希；校验通过时生成当前内容的回执。
docwright 的功能「从素材提取 pack 参数」：调用 doc_extract_params 提交素材和参数候选值，插件核对候选值是否有素材原文引句支持，并保存提取记录供生成时复核。

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · docwright：Document generation for [deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): a pack defines one document type (JSON schema, validation rules, generation prompt), packs chain into multi-stage scenarios, tunable params pass a confirmation gate before generation, every document ships with a replayable validation receipt, and a bundled skill teaches the agent to author new packs.

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · docwright：JSON is the single source of truth. Every generated document is validated against its pack's JSON Schema and rule set; failures are fed back to the model for repair until all rules pass (or the loop exhausts and keeps a red-marked draft). Every document ships with a machine-readable receipt anyone can re-verify.

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · Quickstart (deterministic, ~2 minutes, no API key)：```sh
dsh plugin add @sharework-ai/dsh-docwright   # 1. install the bundle into your profile
dsh                                 # 2. start a session with the profile
```

Copy the bundled sample into your workspace, then in the session:

```
> doc_validate(artifactPath: "sample.json", pack: "cosmic-plan")

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · sample.json = the pack's bundled golden sample copied into your workspace：```

You get an all-green receipt in seconds — zero LLM calls. This is the deterministic first-run moment; `doc_generate` (the closed loop) is step two.

text: @sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · `doc_packs`：Zero-arg discovery tool: lists installed packs as `[{ name, version, description, languages, consumes, params }]` (params = the pack's declared tunables with type, description, optional default, and the `required`/`confirm`/`overridable`/`extractable` flags). The model-facing descriptions of `doc_generate`/`doc_validate` carry a static invitation to call `doc_packs` first; unknown-pack errors also point there. Descriptions never change with the pack set (pull-based progressive disclosure).

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · `doc_generate`：| Parameter | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pack` | string | e.g. `cosmic-plan`; unknown names list available packs |
| `materials` | string[]? | paths relative to the materials root (default `<workspace>/references/`), or inline text starting with `#!inline`; optional for chained packs whose upstream carries the context |
| `language` | string? | default: config `defaultLanguage`, else the pack's first language |
| `upstream` | string[]? | workspace-relative paths to upstream artifacts; each must carry a green sidecar receipt (hash-verified, pack type matched against `consumes`, and recording the installed pack version — see `upstreamVersionPolicy`). Extra green artifacts of installed packs may ride along as prompt context (e.g. the project context beside a plan); at least one consumed type is required |
| `artifactName` | string? | output base name (default `<pack>-<timestamp>`); refused on packs with an `artifactPrefix` (PLAN/REQ/FUNC/TECH) — those are engine-named `<PREFIX>-<topicNo>` (whole-requirement) and `<PREFIX>-<topicNo>-<NN>` (per-function; NN = the two-digit right-aligned targetIndex); topicNo comes from the topic n

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · `doc_generate`：Per-function fan-out (`docs/designs/params-and-chain-contract.md`): chained packs declare a required `targetIndex` (1-based position in the upstream plan's `functions[]`); a missing one fails loud with the full candidate list (index, funcId, l2Name). Calls without an explicit `artifactName` default to `<pack>-<funcId>` (or `<PREFIX>-<topicNo>-<NN>` when the pack declares an `artifactPrefix` — funcId itself is `<topicNo>-<NN>`, numbered by rule plan/func-id-numbering) so distinct functions never collide; results carry a `coverage` line (`{ covered, total, missing }`) showing how much of the reference function set this stage has already produced. `doc_chain_status` gives the whole-chain matrix.

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · `doc_generate`：Returns `{ artifactPath, markdownPath, receipt }`. Artifacts, receipts, and markdown land in the output root (default `<workspace>/output/`, or `<topic>/output/` with `topic`). Exhausted loops throw AND keep the draft + red receipt on disk.

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · `doc_generate`：**Scopes & reuse** (`docs/designs/cosmic-context.md`): packs declare `scope` (`workspace` packs fix their homes — materials `references/`, artifacts `context/` — and ignore `topic`; `topic` scope is the default) and `reuse` (workspace packs default true, topic packs false). For `reuse` packs, a green, hash-intact artifact of the same pack and installed version that was generated from exactly the call's inputs (the receipt records a materials manifest of canonical refs + content hashes; chained packs additionally compare upstream anchors and the addressed artifact name; changed, added, or dropped materials, a regenerated upstream, or a different addressed name regenerate) is returned as-is (`reused: true`, zero LLM); `force: true` always rebuilds — a human-corrected artifact changes the hash and therefore regenerates, and `doc_validate`'s seal (which carries the manifest forward) re-enters it into the chain.

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · `doc_extract_params`：Material param extraction with machine-checkable provenance (`docs/designs/params-and-chain-contract.md`, extract-params). For packs whose manifest marks params `extractable: true` (see `doc_packs`), run this BEFORE `doc_generate`: for each extractable param propose `{ value, quote }` — `quote` must be a verbatim excerpt of the materials (whitespace-insensitive; the engine verifies and refuses unproven values) — or `{ notFound: true }`, optionally with a `suggestion`/`rationale` for the user to endorse (never auto-applied). "Not found" is a first-class result: a required param left notFound is intercepted before generation and must be asked from the user — the materials must not be silently substituted for. Results persist as `<pack>.extracted.json` next to the pack's artifacts; `doc_generate` re-verifies every quote against the generation-time materials, so changed materials invalidate unproven entries, and a re-extracted different value bypasses the reuse pre-check (the receipt's as-run params no longer match) and reaches the confirmation gate.

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · `doc_validate`：Re-runs the ruleset over an existing artifact — deterministic, no LLM. `artifactPath` is workspace-relative (e.g. `output/plan-123.json`). Returns a fresh receipt; a hash mismatch means the artifact changed after generation.

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · `doc_validate`：**Sealing**: a green validation re-issues (seals) the sidecar receipt for the current content (`sealed: true`) — externally edited artifacts that revalidate green rejoin the chain without regeneration. A red validation never touches the sidecar. Results also carry a best-effort artifact `summary` (counts and totalCfps).

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · `doc_validate`：Also returns `packVersionStale`: `true` when the sidecar receipt was written by a different pack version — the artifact predates the installed pack and its green receipt certifies the OLD rules, so regenerate; `false` when versions match; `null` when no receipt exists.

Validation replays by the receipt-recorded as-run pack params (original standards); pass `params` explicitly for what-if checks.

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · `doc_validate`：Chained packs accept an optional `upstream` string[] (the same paths used at generation): it re-runs the green-receipt verification and feeds the parsed artifacts into function rules, so cross-artifact rules (e.g. cosmic-req's plan-alignment) replay too — the fresh receipt then records the `upstreamHashes` anchors. Omitting it leaves those rules failing loud with a message that points here.

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · `doc_chain_status`：Per-function fan-out accounting — deterministic, no LLM. Pass `plan` (workspace-relative path to a green plan artifact); the tool walks the consuming stages via each pack's `consumes`, scans the output root for green per-function artifacts, and returns the coverage matrix: which plan functions have artifacts at which stage, per-stage `{ covered, total }` counts, and any `orphaned` green artifacts whose funcId matches no plan function. Run it before presenting a fan-out chain as complete.

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · Configuration (cordis.yml)：```yaml
- id: docwright
  config:
    packsDir: ""            # extra pack dirs; same-name packs override built-ins
    workspaceRoot: ""       # fallback root when no session workspace (default: cwd)

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · Configuration (cordis.yml)：**Workspace & roots**: the per-call workspace root is the session's workspace directory (the conversation's cwd — e.g. the folder picked in the dsh web UI), falling back to `workspaceRoot`, then the process cwd. `materialsRoot`/`outputRoot` may be relative (joined to the workspace root) or absolute, but must resolve INSIDE the workspace root — anything else fails loud. Material references resolve against `materialsRoot`; artifact writes (and returned `artifactPath` values) live under `outputRoot`. Containment, tamper-evident receipts, and upstream chain verification all hold against the workspace root regardless of root customization. On Linux hosts, Windows drive-letter paths (`D:\x\y` / `d:/x/y`) passed to any path parameter are normalized to their WSL mounts via the `wslpath` binary when available (respecting custom mount roots), with a default-mount regex (`/mnt/<drive>/`) as fallback.

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · Configuration (cordis.yml)：**Provider route names**: `provider` must name a route registered in the host's LLM composition. The bundled `dsh-llm-deepseek` adapter registers as `deepseek-official` (not `deepseek`); `dsh-llm-pi-ai` registers one route per configured provider profile. An unknown route surfaces as an empty stream (`NO_ADAPTER`), not a loud error — if `doc_generate` reports an llm-error on round 1, check the adapter's registered route name first.
@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · Packs：Hybrid packs: declarative JSON rules for simple families, JS functions for cross-field rules.

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · Packs：Six built-in packs cover the COSMIC flow (`cosmic-context` → `cosmic-plan` → `cosmic-req` → `cosmic-func` → `cosmic-tech`, plus `cosmic-context-sync`): context = the workspace-level project context (module tree with codes, roles, third-party systems, ID conventions, design principles; model assumptions explicitly registered), plan = module-change planning (functions hang off modules — one module may carry several; `changeKind` reconciled against the context tree by module name), req = per-function requirements analysis (functional users with kind + user stories — the flow-analysis source — and business rules), func = functional-process design (originator/receiver/origination event per process), tech = the data-movement breakdown whose sequences must follow the three audit-safe patterns `ERX`/`EW`/`EX` (≈2.5 movements per process) and whose total CFPs must never fall below the plan estimate (upper tolerance from the budget's `upFactor`). Downstream stages re-anchor `index`/`funcId`/`desiredCfps` to their parent. `cosmic-context-sync` merges one topic's green plan back into the workspace context so project knowledge evolves with requirements

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · Packs：```
packs/cosmic-plan/
├── manifest.json     # name, version, description (LocalizedText: one line or a {en, zh} map; doc_packs projects the en entry to models), consumes, languages, maxRounds?, params?
├── schema.json       # draft-07 JSON Schema
├── rules/zh-CN.json  # declarative: minLength / maxLength / forbiddenKeywords / pattern (literal regex or { "param": "..." })

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · Packs：**Pack contract:** `manifest.description` is required and names the document this pack generates — a one-line string or a LocalizedText map (`{ "en": ..., "zh": ... }`, en entry mandatory as the fallback; builtin cosmic packs ship both; load-time enforced; `doc_packs` projects the en entry to the model regardless of UI locale); `manifest.params` declares the pack's tunables (declaration IS the allowlist — `{ type: number|string|boolean|object, default?, description (same LocalizedText shape), enum?, min?, max?, required?, overridable?, confirm?, extractable? }` per param; load-time invariants: `overridable` and `extractable` each require `confirm` (an adjustable baseline and an extracted value must both pass the confirmation gate), and params referenced by declarative rules (numeric bounds or pattern sources) must not be `overridable`; `required: true` forbids a default; optional params may omit the default (inherited-or-explicit only); declarative-rule numeric bounds may reference number params and `pattern` rules may reference string params via `{ "param": "name" }` — the referenced param must always be present (default or required), a n

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · Packs：**Pack authoring** is a first-class plugin capability (docs/designs/pack-authoring.md): when no installed pack fits a document type, the model loads the bundled `docwright-pack-authoring` skill (registered at apply time on the host's skills registry; the playbook ships in `guides/`) and walks a nine-stage flow — domain analysis, artifact planning, schema, rules (plain Node-loadable ESM JS in `rules/functions.js`; the built-in severity deduction `100 − 10×error − 3×warning − 1×info` is the default convergence score), params, chain design, verification, registration. The verification shortcut is `pnpm run pack:check -- <packs-dir> [--with <other-root>]...`: the real loader gate plus per-language golden green through the real DocService (chain packs use their consumed packs' golden samples as upstream; `samples/golden.params.json` supplies required-no-default params for the golden run). Local packs install via the `packsDir` config (convention: `<workspace>/.docwright/packs/`); a same-name pack there overrides a built-in one. Packs load at apply time — reload the plugin after writing files.

@sharework-ai/dsh-docwright README · then, in this repo：**Note on devDependencies:** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` packages link to the local `deepseek-harness` checkout via `link:` (a bare symlink: `file:` would try to resolve dsh's `workspace:*` internals, which only resolve inside the dsh workspace). The linked packages' `exports` point at their `lib/` build outputs, hence the one-time dsh build above. `pnpm-workspace.yaml` overrides also align `cordis`/`cosmokit`/`schemastery` with dsh's vendored copies so a single instance of each loads per process. Runtime consumers never install these — they are `peerDependencies` resolved from the host dsh installation. Switch the `link:` entries back to registry versions once dsh publishes a complete release.
